evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:100-110,114-124,157-167,171-181 — the pet/vehicle delete and review (approve) handlers await mutateAsync inside try/catch, but the catch body is ONLY `console.error(...)`. No toast, no setError, no user-facing feedback. When a delete/approve fails (403 from RLS, validation error, network drop) the row simply stays and the user sees nothing — a silent failure on a destructive/state-changing action.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/main.tsx:28-35 — the QueryClient defaultOptions sets only queries.staleTime/retry; there is NO MutationCache onError handler, so mutation rejections are not surfaced globally either. The ErrorBoundary wrapping the tree (main.tsx) catches render errors, not awaited async mutation rejections, so nothing upstream recovers this.

Contrast: the sibling EmergencyContactDirectoryPage.tsx:106-111 handles the identical pattern correctly with `setError(t('emergency.errors.failedToCreate'))` + console.error, confirming the house convention is to surface a user-visible error. RegistryPage regresses from it.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx — the page never imports useTranslation; every user-facing string is hardcoded English. Specifically the native confirm dialogs: line 100 `window.confirm('Are you sure you want to delete this pet registration?')`, line 114 `window.confirm('Approve this pet registration?')`, line 157 and line 171 the vehicle equivalents. The ppt-web app is i18n-enabled (react-i18next, locales sk/cs/de/en per CLAUDE.md), so these strings are untranslatable — an i18n gap, not a cosmetic nit.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:91,95,129,148,152,186 — all navigation (view/edit/create for pets and vehicles) is done with `window.location.href = '/registry/...'`, which triggers a full browser reload: it tears down the SPA, drops in-memory + TanStack Query cache, and re-downloads the Vite bundle on every registry link. The sibling RegistryRulesPage.tsx uses react-router's useNavigate, confirming the project convention; RegistryPage should use useNavigate for client-side routing.
